preview.label: This picture is a tone-mapped SDR approximation of HDR content, not a monitoring reference. It is not calibrated, it is not what the HDR deliverable looks like, and no Kinewright check is a judgment about how it looks. Calibrated HDR monitoring is a separate later programme: CC8 makes no display-capability query and no HDR handoff, so this preview is what an HDR-capable display gets too.
preview.delivery_boundary: Preview only. CC8 §4 item 5: the tone map must not be reachable from the delivery path, and §0.2 Q6 refuses tone-mapped SDR delivery from an HDR timeline as a deliverable.

budgets.gate_bound_rule: bound = max(next_power_of_two(recorded), granularity_floor) × 4. The x4 is cc8_fixtures::CC8_MEASURED_BOUND_HEADROOM, two powers of two, the allowance cc8_hdr's own test bounds make for f32::powf/exp/ln accuracy Rust does not specify across two libm implementations. Nothing in §9.2's table was chosen; every budget is this rule applied to a figure a fixture took.

delivery_constants.note: §9.2: 'None may be invented, scaled, or inherited from another lane.' The HDR lane shares CC6 §4.1's Ten depth and nothing else: its five constants were measured on its own HLG-coded Rec.2020 population. Three differ from the 10-bit SDR lane's and are tighter; the two that coincide do so because both derivations arrived at one delivery code and one delivery code as a mean from different measurements, which cc8_gate_budgets_are_distinct_from_every_neighbouring_constant names rather than hides.

budgets.delivery_note: CC6 owns the two SDR lanes' constants and CC8 never re-baselines one; the HDR lane's five are CC8's own, measured at §10 step 6 and published here at step 10.
budgets.delivery_measured_note: Every 'measured' figure in the Decoded HDR delivery row, and the decoded legality rate beside it, is a Linux measurement (see budgets.measurement) and is reported, not gated: the two CI FFmpeg builds decode the same encode to different numbers (CC7 §0.3 PM-E12, CC6 §0.4), so what gates on both operating systems is the 'budget' column, with the live and this recorded measurement each inside it in the term's own direction. No cfg(windows), no per-OS constant.

delivery_windows_observed.note: Nothing to record yet: every §9.2 figure in this manifest is unmeasured on Windows. CC7's equivalent block carried two MSVC figures because a Windows run had reached them before an equality assertion stopped it; CC8's fixtures gate against constants from the first commit, so a green Windows run publishes no number and a red one would publish a failure. What IS known is that the CC8 fixtures have run green on windows-latest for every step landed through 8 — CI runs 33235031761 (§10 step 1's encoder precondition, §0.3(e)), 33237026987, 33239083483, 33240770490, 33241968697, 33245077348, 33246869396 and 33248465523 — so the tags survive an MSVC libx264 encode and re-probe and every budget above holds there. The step-9 run, 33250611786, was still in flight when step 10 was written. The figures themselves stay Linux figures until a Windows job prints its own CC8_MEASURED lines.
delivery_windows_observed.rule: §14 / R5's form: a per-OS note, never a per-OS constant.

amendments.summary: Draft v1 accepted as written; all six §0.2 recommendations adopted verbatim; the §0.5 roadmap edits applied in the same commit; accepted with Q2's HLG-in-AVC recognition counter-argument outstanding as §12's first risk.

CC8 implemented across §10 steps 1-10; §3.3's HLG stage-naming amended to the realized decode and delivery directions; §9.2's table filled with the measured values; five implementer determinations recorded (fixture 6's 'unchanged', §5.1's intermediate white, §4's preview curve, managed_hdr_v1's timing, and the inventory's declared-set rule).

owner_decisions.Q1: HLG (ARIB STD-B67), Rec.2020, limited range, 10-bit; PQ/HDR10 deferred
owner_decisions.Q2: reuse the existing 10-bit libx264 lane; no HEVC. Accepted with the HLG-in-AVC recognition risk open.
owner_decisions.Q3: no wide-gamut working space; BT.709 primaries and D65 kept, Rec.2020 a named conversion
owner_decisions.Q4: a labelled tone-mapped preview that is not a monitoring reference and carries no exit gate
owner_decisions.Q6: SDR-from-HDR as preview only; HDR-from-SDR refused permanently

determinations.determination: decode = inverse OETF → forward OOTF at the pinned nominal peak and gamma → anchor divide; delivery = inverse OOTF → OETF. §3.3's pipeline listing named the decode-side stage 'HLG inverse OOTF', which is the delivery direction; §0.6 A1 amends the section text to the realized directions.

'unchanged' is measured on whatever build runs the fixture, never against a checked-in digest: every delivery colour term the export handed FFmpeg is asserted character-for-character against the frozen pre-CC8 literals, two exports of one project are byte-identical, and three equivalent spellings export the same bytes. The SHA-256s are printed, never asserted.

65 280 means the HLG signal peak, not diffuse white. §5.1 keeps the convention unchanged and unmeasured; its HDR meaning had to be determined, and it is gated with a bound derived from the half-nit argument through the OOTF and OETF slopes.

§4 names properties, not a curve. Extended Reinhard at §2.2's own pinned HLG nominal peak was chosen — no new number, one parameter asserted equal to the existing constant — applied per channel in linear light before the unchanged BT.709 monitor encode, from IEEE-exact operations only so determinism is bitwise on both operating systems.

§7's state lands at step 9 rather than step 3, because the lane it names did not exist until step 6. It is never stamped by a load; only the ordinary undoable revision-gated SetColorContext writes it, so a pre-CC8 project holding a Rec.2020 delivery description CC6 refused cannot silently become HDR-exportable on first open.

A test is CC8's if CC8 wrote it. 95 carry the cc8_ prefix; 10 were written into #[cfg(test)] mod tests blocks that predate CC8, where the local convention is unprefixed, and are named explicitly under CC7 §11.3's 'or be named explicitly in the inventory'. Tests of CC1-CC7 whose tuples CC8 moved keep their own contract's inventory.
